title: Gai Thod – Thai Fried Chicken

items: 1 kg chicken drumsticks or mid-joint wings (skin-on, bone-in preferred)
2 tbsp coriander root (or stems), finely pounded
2 tbsp tempura flour (optional, for extra crisp)

instructions.title: 1. Marinate the Chicken
steps: Pound garlic, coriander root, and white pepper into a paste (classic Thai trinity for marinades).
Mix with fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and salt.
Coat chicken thoroughly, cover, and marinate for at least 4 hours (preferably overnight).

instructions.title: 2. Prepare the Coating
steps: Mix rice flour, tapioca flour, tempura flour, baking powder, white pepper, and salt in a large bowl.
Lightly dredge marinated chicken in the flour mixture just before frying. Shake off excess.

instructions.title: 3. Fry the Aromatics
steps: Heat neutral oil in a wok/pot to 160–170°C (320–340°F).
Add sliced garlic and shallots, fry until golden and crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels. Reserve for garnish.

instructions.title: 4. Fry the Chicken
steps: Fry chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through (12–15 minutes depending on size).
Remove and rest on a rack (not paper towels, to preserve crispness).

instructions.title: 5. Serve
steps: Top chicken with crispy fried garlic and shallots.
Serve with sticky rice (khao neow) and Nam Jim Jaew dipping sauce.
Garnish with cucumber slices and fresh herbs for restaurant-style plating.

tips: Double Fry for Extra Crunch: Fry once at 160°C, rest, then fry again briefly at 180°C before serving.
Balance Flavor: The marinade should be garlicky, peppery, salty-sweet with umami depth from fish sauce.
Presentation: Serve on a banana leaf with small bowls of dipping sauces for authenticity.
Pairing: Excellent with Som Tum (papaya salad) and sticky rice for a full Thai dining experience.
